# Project integration sizing contract

Do not migrate gameplay into project.html until the user approves it.

## Characters

Use scene-metrics.js in both the development preview and the eventual project renderer:

- Normal player/NPC sprite area: 89.6 CSS/world pixels.
- Boss sprite area: 268.8 CSS/world pixels.
- Shared sprite display padding: 5.6 pixels.

These values approximate the apparent size of the former 130/260-pixel actors after the old 1280-pixel canvas was displayed at roughly 1108 pixels wide. Actual visible artwork size still depends on each sheet's referenceSize and transparent padding. Preserve those per-sheet settings and source crops. Do not multiply character size by browser width, fullscreen size, or map zoom.

viewport.js sets canvas dimensions to its displayed CSS dimensions. This makes one world unit equal one displayed pixel; larger views reveal more world. Reuse it in the project screen. Keep the CSS canvas dimensions explicitly controlled by the viewport/container. If high-DPI rendering is added later, apply devicePixelRatio to the backing buffer/context only; keep world and collision coordinates in CSS pixels.

## Maps

- Playarea 1: scale background to viewport height; horizontal scroll only.
- Playarea 2: scale background to viewport width; vertical scroll only.
- Playarea 3: retain fixed world tile dimensions, overlap, seed, and source collision scale. Larger viewports display more tiles without enlarging them.
- Playarea 4: retain islandScale and finite image world dimensions. Larger viewports reveal more of the island; do not automatically fit/stretch the island to fullscreen.

Player/NPC rendering, collision footprints, placement bounds, tower occlusion, and arrow positioning use the same shared character size defaults. NPCs cloned from player sheets still use NPC movement speeds. Keep this distinction when implementing the future player character picker.

## Agreed game viewport reference
Use a centered 1280x720 game area on the user's 1920x1080 display, matching the supplied screenshot. Keep fixed character sizes; do not stretch the view to fill 1920x1080. The Development Preview Game Area button demonstrates this layout with a dark surround. Fit smaller browser windows at 16:9 while keeping one world pixel equal to one CSS pixel. Project migration still requires the user's instruction.

import { getFirebaseAuth } from '../firebase-client.js';
import { isAdmin } from '../admin-access.js';
import { isGuestSession } from '../guest-session.js';

/** Reveal development content only after Firebase confirms the admin session. */
export async function requireAdmin() {
  const content = document.querySelector('#development-content');
  if (isGuestSession()) {
    content.hidden = true;
    window.location.replace('../project.html');
    return false;
  }

  try {
    const { auth, sdk } = await getFirebaseAuth();

    return await new Promise(resolve => {
      sdk.onAuthStateChanged(auth, user => {
        const allowed = isAdmin(user);
        content.hidden = !allowed;

        if (!allowed) {
          window.location.replace(user ? '../project.html' : '../index.html');
        }

        resolve(allowed);
      }, () => {
        content.hidden = true;
        window.location.replace('../index.html');
        resolve(false);
      });
    });
  } catch {
    content.hidden = true;
    window.location.replace('../index.html');

579:  arisu:{interval:8,chargeUpSeconds:2,chargeSpeed:1100,recoverySeconds:.6},
import { enemyContactDamageFormula } from './game-config.js';
import { yuukaSettings } from './game-config.js';
import { contactSettings } from './game-config.js';
export { contactSettings } from './game-config.js';
import { getCombatHitbox } from './combat-hitboxes.js';
import { damagePlayer } from './player-stats.js';
import { beginKnockback, advanceKnockback } from './knockback.js';

// Contact reaction settings live in game-config.js.
/** Detect player pass-through with a swept segment rather than endpoint overlap only. */
function contactGeometry(npc, player, motion) {
  const enemyBody = getCombatHitbox(npc, true), playerBody = getCombatHitbox(player, false);
  const rx = enemyBody.rx + playerBody.rx, ry = enemyBody.ry + playerBody.ry;
  const fromX = playerBody.x - motion.x, fromY = playerBody.y - motion.y;
  const lengthSquared = motion.x * motion.x + motion.y * motion.y;
  const scaledLength = (motion.x / rx) ** 2 + (motion.y / ry) ** 2;
  const t = scaledLength ? Math.max(0, Math.min(1,
    ((enemyBody.x - fromX) * motion.x / rx ** 2 +
      (enemyBody.y - fromY) * motion.y / ry ** 2) / scaledLength)) : 1;
  const dx = enemyBody.x - (fromX + motion.x * t);
  const dy = enemyBody.y - (fromY + motion.y * t);
  const distance = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
  const pushing = lengthSquared > 0.0001 &&
    motion.x * (npc.x - fromX) + motion.y * (npc.y - fromY) > 0;
  // At exact overlap, push along player travel; otherwise away from the player.
  const fallbackLength = Math.hypot(motion.x, motion.y) || 1;
  const nx = distance > 0.001 ? dx / distance : lengthSquared ? motion.x / fallbackLength : 1;
  const ny = distance > 0.001 ? dy / distance : lengthSquared ? motion.y / fallbackLength : 0;
  const radius = 1 / Math.hypot(nx / rx, ny / ry);
  return { touching: (dx / rx) ** 2 + (dy / ry) ** 2 < 1, pushing, radius, nx, ny,
    overlap: Math.max(0, radius - Math.hypot(enemyBody.x - playerBody.x, enemyBody.y - playerBody.y)) };
}

/** React to contact, flash once, and pause chase until bounce/push recovery ends. */
export function updateNpcContact(npc, player, motion, delta, move, survivalSeconds = 0) {
  npc.contactCooldown = Math.max(0, (npc.contactCooldown || 0) - delta);
  // Per-enemy attack cooldown is separate from recoil and the player's global I-frames.
  npc.playerHitCooldown = Math.max(0, (npc.playerHitCooldown || 0) - delta);
  const hit = contactGeometry(npc, player, motion);
  if (hit.touching && !(player.contactIFrames > 0) && !(npc.playerHitCooldown > 0)) {
    const baseDamage = npc.contactDamage ?? (npc.type === 'mob' ? contactSettings.mobDamage : contactSettings.playerDamage);
    const damage = npc.perTypeStats ? Math.floor(baseDamage * (npc.contactDamageMultiplier ?? 1)) :
      enemyContactDamageFormula(baseDamage, player.level || 1, survivalSeconds, npc.contactDamageMultiplier ?? 1);
    const damaged = damagePlayer(player, damage);
    if (damaged && npc.type === 'yuuka') npc.playerHitCooldown = yuukaSettings.contactHitInterval;
    if (damaged) player.contactIFrames = contactSettings.iFrameDuration;
  }
  const overrideBounce = npc.contactReaction?.kind === 'bounce' && hit.pushing;
  if (hit.touching && ((!npc.contactReaction && !npc.contactCooldown) || overrideBounce)) {
    const kind = hit.pushing ? 'push' : 'bounce';
    const settings = contactSettings[kind];
    const overlap = hit.overlap;
    const knockback = beginKnockback(npc, hit.nx * (settings.distance + overlap),
      hit.ny * (settings.distance + overlap), settings.travel);
    npc.contactReaction = knockback ? { ...knockback, kind, nx: hit.nx, ny: hit.ny } : null;
    if (!knockback) npc.contactCooldown = contactSettings.cooldown;
    npc.attack = null;
  }
  const reaction = npc.contactReaction;
  if (!reaction) return false;
  const settings = contactSettings[reaction.kind];
  advanceKnockback(npc, reaction, delta, move);
  const pauseChase = npc.contactRecoveryDelay !== false;
  if (pauseChase) npc.moving = false;
  const recovery = pauseChase ? settings.recovery : settings.travel;
  if (reaction.elapsed >= recovery) {
    npc.contactReaction = null;
    npc.contactCooldown = contactSettings.cooldown;
  }
  // Bosses still recoil/flash, but do not skip their AI update or wait afterward.
  return pauseChase;
}

/** Endless arrivals use these exact base values, without reapplying Mega HP/ATK bonuses. */
export const endlessEnemySettings = {
  startSeconds: 23 * 60, midoriStartSeconds: 30 * 60,
  mega: { hp: 5000, atk: 15, spd: 1, exp: 25 },
  midori: { hp: 9000, atk: 5, spd: 1.5, exp: 25 },
  enemies: [...mobs, 'pedrozilla', ...arius, ...highlanders, ...sweepers]
};

/** Return an ordinary arrival profile; Midori joins the evenly mixed pool at 30:00. */
export function pickEndlessEnemy(seconds, random = Math.random) {
  const settings = endlessEnemySettings;
  if (seconds < settings.startSeconds) return null;
  const pool = seconds >= settings.midoriStartSeconds ? [...settings.enemies, 'midori'] : settings.enemies;
  const type = pool[Math.min(pool.length - 1, Math.floor(random() * pool.length))];
  const mega = type !== 'midori';
  return {type, mega:false, scheduled:false,
    row:{id:`endless-${type}`, stage:'endless', kind:'regular', enemies:[type],
      ...(mega ? settings.mega : settings.midori), mega, endless:true, start:settings.startSeconds}};
}

import { basicMobHpFormula, eliteChanceFormula } from './game-config.js';
import { standardEnemyWeights, enemyStagePools, enemyTypeStats, playerSettings, enemyStatsScalingFormula, campaignScalingTimeFormula } from './game-config.js';
import { combatBalance } from './game-config.js';
import { eliteSizeMultiplier, eliteChance, mobBaseHp, shirokoBossStats } from './game-config.js';
export { eliteSizeMultiplier, eliteChance, mobBaseHp, shirokoBossStats } from './game-config.js';
import { normalSpriteSize } from './scene-metrics.js';

// Elite size, HP and spawn chance are configured in game-config.js.





/** Roll basic-enemy elites; bosses and playable-character test NPCs are excluded. */
export function enemyVariant(type, template, mode = 'random', random = Math.random, survivalSeconds = 0, endlessSeconds = null, eliteProbability = eliteChanceFormula(endlessSeconds)) {
  const elite = template.miniBoss === true || type === 'midori' || (type === 'mob' || template.standard) && (mode === 'elite' || (mode === 'random' && random() < eliteProbability));
  const baseHp = (['mob', 'midori'].includes(type) || template.standard) ? basicMobHpFormula(survivalSeconds)
    : type === 'shiroko' ? mobBaseHp * shirokoBossStats.hpMultiplier : combatBalance.otherEnemyHp;
  const megaType = type === 'megaMob' || (type === 'mob' && elite) ? 'megaMob' :
    type === 'megaSweeper' || (['whiteSweeper','heavySweeper'].includes(type) && elite) ? 'megaSweeper' : null;
  const dedicatedMega = Boolean(megaType);
  const profile = enemyTypeStats[megaType || type];
  const scaled = profile ? enemyStatsScalingFormula(profile, campaignScalingTimeFormula(endlessSeconds)) : null;
  const maxHp = (scaled?.hp ?? baseHp) * (elite && !dedicatedMega ? combatBalance.eliteHpMultiplier : 1);
  return {
    elite,
    miniBoss: template.miniBoss === true || (elite && type !== 'midori'),
    label: dedicatedMega ? (megaType === 'megaSweeper' ? 'Mega Sweeper' : 'Mega Mob') : elite && type !== 'midori' ? `Mega ${template.label}` : template.label,
    spriteSize: (template.spriteSize || normalSpriteSize) * (elite && type !== 'midori' && !template.miniBoss ? (template.megaSizeMultiplier ?? eliteSizeMultiplier) : 1),
    hp: maxHp,
    maxHp,
    contactDamage: type === 'shiroko' ? shirokoBossStats.contactDamage : template.contactDamage,
    contactDamageMultiplier: elite && !dedicatedMega ? 2 : 1,
    ...(profile ? { hp: Math.round(maxHp), maxHp: Math.round(maxHp), perTypeStats: true,
      contactDamage: scaled.atk, expReward: profile.expValue,
      movementSpeedMultiplier: scaled.spd * playerSettings.speed / playerSettings.movementBase } : {})
  };
}

/** Pick from the configured standard enemy pool while keeping Mob most common. */
export function chooseStandardEnemy(random = Math.random, elapsedSeconds = 0, stageId = null) {
  const weights = stageId && enemyStagePools[stageId] ? Object.fromEntries(enemyStagePools[stageId].map(type=>[type,1])) : standardEnemyWeights;
  const entries = Object.entries(weights).filter(([type, weight]) => {
    const profile = enemyTypeStats[type];
    return weight > 0 && (!profile || (elapsedSeconds >= profile.spawnStartSeconds && elapsedSeconds < profile.spawnEndSeconds));
  });
  let roll = random() * entries.reduce((sum, [, weight]) => sum + weight, 0);
  for (const [type, weight] of entries) { roll -= weight; if (roll < 0) return type; }
  return entries.at(-1)?.[0] ?? null;
}

/** Calculate a score snapshot with timer components, preserving the supplied hour rules.
 * Hardcore is opt-in; this helper does not implement a Hardcore game mode or publish scores.
 */
export function scoreFormula({ enemyDefeated = 0, miniBossDefeated = 0, bossDefeated = 0,
  playerLevel = 1, elapsedSeconds = 0, hardcore = false } = {}) {
  const seconds = Math.max(0, Math.floor(elapsedSeconds));
  const finalHourValue = Math.floor(seconds / 3600);
  const finalMinuteValue = Math.floor(seconds / 60) % 60;
  const finalSecondValue = seconds % 60;
  const s = scoreSettings;
  const baseScore = enemyDefeated * s.enemy + miniBossDefeated * s.miniBoss + bossDefeated * s.boss +
    Math.max(0, finalMinuteValue - 30) * s.minutePast30 + Math.min(59, finalMinuteValue) * s.minute +
    Math.min(59, finalSecondValue) * s.second + playerLevel * s.level;
  const hardcoreBonus = hardcore ? Math.floor(baseScore *
    (finalMinuteValue * s.hardcoreMinute + finalHourValue * s.hardcoreHour)) : 0;
  return { baseScore, hardcoreBonus, finalScore: Math.floor(baseScore + hardcoreBonus) };
}

import { stageProgressionSettings } from './game-config.js';

/** Progress the campaign in order, then choose a different available map per boss wave. */
export function nextStageAfterBoss(currentMap, endless, availableMaps, random = Math.random) {
  const settings = stageProgressionSettings;
  const regular = settings.order.filter(id => availableMaps.includes(id));
  const index = settings.order.indexOf(currentMap);
  if (!endless && index >= 0 && index < settings.order.length - 1) {
    const next = settings.order.slice(index + 1).find(id => availableMaps.includes(id));
    return { mapId: next || currentMap, endless: false, secretRolled: false };
  }
  const secretRolled = random() < settings.secretChance;
  if (secretRolled && availableMaps.includes(settings.secretStageId)) {
    return { mapId: settings.secretStageId, endless: true, secretRolled: true };
  }
  // An unimplemented secret stage falls back to a real map, without creating assets or routes.
  const choices = regular.filter(id => id !== currentMap);
  const pool = choices.length ? choices : regular;
  return { mapId: pool[Math.floor(random() * pool.length)] || currentMap,
    endless: true, secretRolled };
}

/** A wave ends only on an actual boss defeat with no living or queued bosses remaining. */
export function bossWaveIsDefeated(defeatedEnemy, enemies, hasQueuedBosses) {
  const boss = enemy => enemy.boss === true || (enemy.boss !== false && ['shiroko', 'iroha'].includes(enemy.type));
  return boss(defeatedEnemy) && !hasQueuedBosses && !enemies.some(boss);
}

import { playerSettings, eliteSizeMultiplier, normalSpriteSize } from './game-config.js';
import { campaignSettings, campaignEnemyRows } from './campaign-config.js';

/** Own the internal chart clock; survival time and gameplay continue during clock freezes. */
export function createCampaignSchedule() {
 let stage='first',seconds=campaignSettings.stageStarts.first;
 let spawned=new Set(),defeated=new Set();
 const rows=()=>campaignEnemyRows.filter(row=>row.stage===stage);
 const required=()=>rows().filter(row=>row.kind==='boss'||row.gate);
 const cleared=()=>required().length>0 && required().every(row=>defeated.has(row.id));
 const fighting=()=>rows().some(row=>(row.kind==='boss'||row.gate)&&spawned.has(row.id)&&!defeated.has(row.id));
 const frozen=()=>rows().some(row=>row.freeze&&seconds>=row.start)&&!cleared();
 return {
  get seconds(){return seconds;},get stage(){return stage;},get frozen(){return frozen();},
  get fightingBoss(){return fighting();},get cleared(){return cleared();},
  get readyToAdvance(){return cleared()&&(stage!=='second'||seconds>=campaignSettings.stageStarts.third);},
  setStage(id){if(id===stage)return;stage=id;seconds=campaignSettings.stageStarts[id]??0;spawned=new Set();defeated=new Set();},
  update(delta,spawnEncounter){
   if(!frozen()) {
    const next=seconds+Math.max(0,delta);
    const gate=rows().filter(row=>row.freeze&&!defeated.has(row.id)&&row.start>=seconds).sort((a,b)=>a.start-b.start)[0];
    seconds=gate?Math.min(next,gate.start):next;
   }
   for(const row of rows()) if(row.kind!=='regular'&&seconds>=row.start&&!spawned.has(row.id)) {
    if(spawnEncounter(row))spawned.add(row.id);
   }
  },
  profileFor(type){return rows().filter(row=>row.enemies.includes(type)&&row.start<=seconds).at(-1) || rows().find(row=>row.enemies.includes(type)) || null;},
  recordDefeat(enemy){if(enemy.campaignRowId)defeated.add(enemy.campaignRowId);},
  /** Ordinary selection keeps running while the internal chart clock is frozen. */
  pickSpawn(random=Math.random){
   let pool=rows().filter(row=>row.kind==='regular'&&seconds>=row.start&&seconds<row.end);
   if(stage==='fourth'&&seconds>=campaignSettings.endlessRandomFrom) {
    const latest=new Map();
    for(const row of campaignEnemyRows.filter(r=>r.kind==='regular')) for(const type of row.enemies)latest.set(type,{...row,enemies:[type]});
    pool=[...latest.values()];
   }
   if(!pool.length) pool=rows().filter(row=>row.kind==='regular'&&seconds>=row.start).slice(-1);
   if(!pool.length)return null;
   let row=pool[Math.min(pool.length-1,Math.floor(random()*pool.length))];
   const type=row.enemies[Math.min(row.enemies.length-1,Math.floor(random()*row.enemies.length))];
   let enemy=type,mega=Boolean(row.mega);
   if(fighting()&&random()<campaignSettings.megaChanceDuringBoss){
    const dedicated=rows().find(r=>r.kind==='mini'&&r.baseEnemy===type);
    if(dedicated){row=dedicated;enemy=dedicated.enemies[0];}else mega=true;
   }
   return {row,type:enemy,mega,scheduled:false};
  }
 };
}


/** Exact chart stats override legacy stage/type multipliers; only random Mega rolls add bonuses. */
export function campaignEnemyOverrides(entry, template, baseMovementSpeed = playerSettings.movementBase) {
 const row=entry.row;
 const boosted=Boolean(entry.mega && !row.mega);
 return {label:boosted?`Mega ${template.label || 'Enemy'}`:template.label, hp:row.hp*(boosted?10:1),maxHp:row.hp*(boosted?10:1),
  contactDamage:row.atk*(boosted?2:1),contactDamageMultiplier:1,
  movementSpeedMultiplier:row.spd*playerSettings.speed/baseMovementSpeed,
  expReward:row.exp,perTypeStats:true,
  miniBoss:row.kind==='mini'||Boolean(row.mega)||boosted,boss:row.kind==='boss',
  elite:row.kind==='mini'||Boolean(row.mega)||boosted,
  spriteSize:(template.spriteSize||normalSpriteSize)*((boosted||row.endless&&row.mega)&&!template.miniBoss?(template.megaSizeMultiplier ?? eliteSizeMultiplier):1),
  campaignRowId:entry.scheduled?row.id:null,campaignGuardian:Boolean(row.gate),campaignOverride:true};
}

  function spawn(x,y,forceType){if(drops.size>=fileSettings.maxGround)return false;const point=safeDropLanding(x,y);if(!point)return false;const drop={id:++nextId,...point,forceType};drops.set(drop.id,drop);return drop;}
  return {ready,spawn,get active(){return active;},get count(){return drops.size;},
    roll(enemy){return (enemy.boss===true||['shiroko','iroha','arisu','neru'].includes(enemy.type))&&fileSettings.bossGuaranteed?spawn(enemy.x,enemy.y):false;},
    update(player,previous){if(active)return;const body=getCombatHitbox(player,false);for(const drop of drops.values())if(segmentHitsBody({x:drop.x,y:drop.y,rx:22+body.rx,ry:22+body.ry},previous?.x??player.x,previous?.y??player.y,body.x,body.y)){open(drop);break;}},
    draw(context,camera){if(!image.naturalWidth)return;for(const drop of drops.values()){const x=drop.x-camera.x,y=drop.y-camera.y;if(x<-30||y<-30||x>canvas.width+30||y>canvas.height+30)continue;context.drawImage(image,x-22,y-22,44,44);}},
    clear(){drops.clear();if(active)close();}};
}
  if (!mapTransition || mapTransition.active || !maps.first.image) return;
  planaSkill?.reset();
  arisAttack?.reset();
  luminousAttack?.reset();
  princessAttack?.reset();
  princessSkill?.reset();
  // Snapshot BACKGROUND ONLY. Characters, NPCs, and aim graphics are drawn later.
  context.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
  drawPlayarea();
  const outgoingMap = currentMap;
  mapTransition.begin(layer => drawPlayarea(layer, outgoingMap));
  const player = characters[selected];
  // Retain the current camera origin and player screen position on the new axis.
  cameraAnchor.x = player.x - camera.x;
  cameraAnchor.y = player.y - camera.y;
  const mapOrder = ['first', 'second', 'third', 'fourth'].filter(id => !maps[id].disabled);
  const requested = typeof targetMap === 'string' && maps[targetMap] && !maps[targetMap].disabled
    ? targetMap : mapOrder[(mapOrder.indexOf(currentMap) + 1) % mapOrder.length];
  if (currentMap !== requested) stageEnteredAt = survivalClock.seconds;
  currentMap = requested;
  if (campaignSettings.enabled && !endlessMode) campaignSchedule.setStage(currentMap);
  if (currentMap === 'fourth' && !maps.fourth.placed) {
    // Anchor the island's open central plaza under the player on first entry.
    // This positions the MAP, preserving existing player/NPC world coordinates.
    maps.fourth.originX = player.x - 740 * islandScale;
    maps.fourth.originY = player.y + (player.spriteSize || spriteSize) / 2 - spritePadding - 620 * islandScale;
    maps.fourth.placed = true;
  }
  // Align the new map on its locked axis at the retained camera origin.
  if (maps[currentMap].axis === 'vertical') maps[currentMap].originX = camera.x;
  else if (maps[currentMap].axis === 'horizontal') maps[currentMap].originY = camera.y;
  updateCamera();
  npcTools?.cleanup();
  expPickups?.clear();
  crafters?.clear();
  goldenCrafters?.clear();
  awaitingFileStageAdvance=false;
  gachaFiles?.clear();
  mapAudio?.setMap(currentMap);
  // Keep held inputs, attack timers, AI and aiming live throughout the transition.
  document.querySelector('#switch-map').textContent = `Switch map (current: ${maps[currentMap].label})`;
  return true;
}

/** Yuuka spawn HP: round((normal player damage + 100) / 100 * 900). */
export const yuukaHpSettings = { offset: 100, divisor: 100, base: 900 };
export function yuukaHpFormula(damage) {
  return Math.max(1, Math.round((Math.max(0, damage) + yuukaHpSettings.offset) /
    yuukaHpSettings.divisor * yuukaHpSettings.base));
}

/** ATK/SPD/PICKUP/Haste percent bonus multiplier (25% -> 1.25). */
export function percentBonusFormula(percent) {
  return 1 + Math.max(0, Number.isFinite(Number(percent)) ? Number(percent) : 0) / 100;
}

/** Crowd-adjusted arrivals: 8/s empty -> 5/s at40 nearby; 2/s at50 visible slots. */
export function spawnRateFormula(nearby, visible) {
  const s = playtestSpawnSettings;
  if (visible >= s.visibleLimit) return s.crowdedPerSecond;
  return Math.round(s.perSecond + (s.maxPerSecond - s.perSecond) *
    (1 - Math.min(1, nearby / s.nearbyTarget)));
}

import { timedEnemyEvents, playerSettings } from './game-config.js';

/** Filled circular cluster: golden-angle spacing avoids square rows and hollow rings. */
export function clusterSpawnPoints(anchor, count, spacing) {
  const radius=spacing*Math.sqrt(Math.max(0,count-1))/2;
  const goldenAngle=Math.PI*(3-Math.sqrt(5));
  return Array.from({length:count},(_,i)=>{
    const distance=count>1?radius*Math.sqrt(i/(count-1)):0;
    const angle=i*goldenAngle;
    return {x:anchor.x+Math.cos(angle)*distance,y:anchor.y+Math.sin(angle)*distance};
  });
}

/** Place each scheduled formation once; retry invalid anchors/full capacity without duplicates. */
export function createTimedEnemyEvents(getPoints, spawn, events = timedEnemyEvents, warn = () => {}) {
  const pending = new Map();
  return { update(seconds) {
    for (const event of events) {
      if (seconds<event.timeSeconds-(event.warningSeconds || 0)) continue;
      let state=pending.get(event.id);
      if (!state) { state={index:0,points:null};pending.set(event.id,state); }
      if (event.lifetimeSeconds != null && seconds >= event.timeSeconds+event.lifetimeSeconds) {
        state.index=event.count; continue;
      }
      if (state.index>=event.count) continue;
      state.points ??= getPoints(event);
      if (!state.points) continue;
      if (seconds<event.timeSeconds) {
        if (!state.warned) { warn(event,state.points);state.warned=true; }
        continue;
      }
      while (state.index<event.count) {
        if (!spawn(event,state.points[state.index])) break;
        state.index++;
      }
    }
  }};
}


/** Lock a horde's course at spawn; it never homes toward later player positions. */
export function hordeMotion(enemy) {
  const angle = enemy.chargeAngle ?? 0;
  const directions=['right','downRight','down','downLeft','left','upLeft','up','upRight'];
  return {direction:directions[(Math.round(angle/(Math.PI/4))+8)%8],
    target:{x:enemy.x+Math.cos(angle)*10000,y:enemy.y+Math.sin(angle)*10000}};
}

import { percentBonusFormula, attackDamageFormula, weaponDamageFormula, growthSettings, totalATKFormula, attackStatSettings, totalCritModFormula, bonusDamageTakenFormula, damageBonusFormula, damageReductionFormula, haloDamageFormula, damageModifiersFormula } from './game-config.js';
import { defaultCombatStats, combatBalance } from './game-config.js';
export { defaultCombatStats } from './game-config.js';
// Percent bonuses: zero keeps base values. CRIT is a direct chance percentage.


/** Initialize independent per-character combat stats without resetting upgrades. */
export function ensureCombatStats(character) {
  character.combatStats ??= {};
  character.combatStats.damageBonusMultipliers ??= [];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(defaultCombatStats)) character.combatStats[key] ??= value;
  return character.combatStats;
}

/** Convert a bonus percentage to a multiplier (25% means 1.25 times base). */
export function statMultiplier(character, key) {
  const value = Number(ensureCombatStats(character)[key]);
  if (key === 'atkPercent') return totalCharacterATK(character) / 100;
  return percentBonusFormula(value);
}

/** Roll per-hit critical chance; target debuffs add percentage points before clamping. */
export function rollAttackDamage(character, totalWeaponDamage, random = Math.random,
  { damageMod = 1, forceCritical = false, targetCritBonus = 0, criticalMultiplier, weaponCritDamagePercent = 0, target } = {}) {
  const stats = ensureCombatStats(character);
  const buffs=Object.values(character.combatBuffs||{}).filter(Boolean);
  const bonusCrit=buffs.reduce((sum,buff)=>sum+(Number(buff.critPercent)||0),0);
  const critical = forceCritical || random() < Math.max(0, Math.min(100, stats.critPercent + bonusCrit + targetCritBonus)) / 100;
  const combinedModifier = damageModifiersFormula({
    criticalMultiplier: critical ? characterCriticalMultiplier(character, criticalMultiplier, weaponCritDamagePercent) : 1,
    bonusDamageTaken: bonusDamageTakenFormula(target?.bonusDamageTakenPercent ?? []),
    DB: damageBonusFormula([...stats.damageBonusMultipliers,...buffs.map(buff=>buff.damageBonusMultiplier).filter(Number.isFinite)]),
    DR: damageReductionFormula(target?.damageReductionPercent ?? []),
    halo: characterHaloMultiplier(character, target),
    attackModifier: damageMod // Attack-specific effects, including EX drawing accuracy.
  });
  return { damage: attackDamageFormula(totalWeaponDamage, totalCharacterATK(character), combinedModifier, random),
    critical, type: critical ? 'critical' : 'normal' };
}

import { playerSettings, eliteSizeMultiplier, normalSpriteSize } from './game-config.js';
import { campaignSettings, campaignEnemyRows } from './campaign-config.js';

/** Own the internal chart clock; survival time and gameplay continue during clock freezes. */
export function createCampaignSchedule() {
 let stage='first',seconds=campaignSettings.stageStarts.first;
 let spawned=new Set(),defeated=new Set();
 const rows=()=>campaignEnemyRows.filter(row=>row.stage===stage);
 const required=()=>rows().filter(row=>row.kind==='boss'||row.gate);
 const cleared=()=>required().length>0 && required().every(row=>defeated.has(row.id));
 const fighting=()=>rows().some(row=>(row.kind==='boss'||row.gate)&&spawned.has(row.id)&&!defeated.has(row.id));
 const frozen=()=>rows().some(row=>row.freeze&&seconds>=row.start)&&!cleared();
 return {
  get seconds(){return seconds;},get stage(){return stage;},get frozen(){return frozen();},
  get fightingBoss(){return fighting();},get cleared(){return cleared();},
  get readyToAdvance(){return cleared()&&(stage!=='second'||seconds>=campaignSettings.stageStarts.third);},
  setStage(id){if(id===stage)return;stage=id;seconds=campaignSettings.stageStarts[id]??0;spawned=new Set();defeated=new Set();},
  update(delta,spawnEncounter){
   if(!frozen()) {
    const next=seconds+Math.max(0,delta);
    const gate=rows().filter(row=>row.freeze&&!defeated.has(row.id)&&row.start>=seconds).sort((a,b)=>a.start-b.start)[0];
    seconds=gate?Math.min(next,gate.start):next;
   }
   for(const row of rows()) if(row.kind!=='regular'&&seconds>=row.start&&!spawned.has(row.id)) {
    if(spawnEncounter(row))spawned.add(row.id);
   }
  },
  profileFor(type){return rows().filter(row=>row.enemies.includes(type)&&row.start<=seconds).at(-1) || rows().find(row=>row.enemies.includes(type)) || null;},
  recordDefeat(enemy){if(enemy.campaignRowId)defeated.add(enemy.campaignRowId);},
  /** Ordinary selection keeps running while the internal chart clock is frozen. */
  pickSpawn(random=Math.random){
   let pool=rows().filter(row=>row.kind==='regular'&&seconds>=row.start&&seconds<row.end);
   if(stage==='fourth'&&seconds>=campaignSettings.endlessRandomFrom) {
    const latest=new Map();
    for(const row of campaignEnemyRows.filter(r=>r.kind==='regular')) for(const type of row.enemies)latest.set(type,{...row,enemies:[type]});
    pool=[...latest.values()];
   }
   if(!pool.length) pool=rows().filter(row=>row.kind==='regular'&&seconds>=row.start).slice(-1);
   if(!pool.length)return null;
   let row=pool[Math.min(pool.length-1,Math.floor(random()*pool.length))];
    if (activeCharacter.animationFrames) activeCharacter.gifElapsed = (activeCharacter.gifElapsed || 0) + delta * 1000 * (activeCharacter.animationSpeed || 1);
    if (activeCharacter.transition) activeCharacter.transition.elapsed += delta * 1000;
    const playerBefore = { x: activeCharacter.x, y: activeCharacter.y };
    updateCharacter(activeCharacter, delta, direction);
    const playerMotion = { x: activeCharacter.x - playerBefore.x, y: activeCharacter.y - playerBefore.y };
    updateCamera(delta);
    npcTools?.cleanup(); // Reclaim distant/invalid NPC slots before the next spawn batch.
    if (campaignSettings.enabled && !endlessMode && !pendingStageTransition && !isPlayerDefeated(activeCharacter)) {
      campaignSchedule.update(delta, row=>Boolean(playtestSpawner?.running)&&npcTools.spawnCampaignEncounter(row));
      if(campaignSchedule.readyToAdvance) advanceStageAfterClear();
    }
    const campaignStatus=document.querySelector('#campaign-clock-status');
    if(campaignStatus) campaignStatus.textContent=`Internal chart: ${Math.floor(campaignSchedule.seconds/60)}:${String(Math.floor(campaignSchedule.seconds)%60).padStart(2,'0')}${campaignSchedule.frozen?' (frozen)':''}`;

 const groups=new Map(),prepared=new Map();
 const ended=new Set();
 const finish=group=>{if(ended.has(group.event.id))return;ended.add(group.event.id);onEnd(group.event.id);groups.delete(group.event.id);};
 function start(event,internalSeconds,stage,points=null,delay=0){
  if(ended.has(event.id)||groups.has(event.id))return;
  const actual={...event,groupId:event.id,runtimeManaged:true};
  groups.set(event.id,{event:actual,stage,started:active+delay,nextWave:0,waves:[],points,announced:false});
 }
 function runGroup(group,internalSeconds,stage,enabled){
  const e=group.event,age=active-group.started;
  if(e.lifetimeSeconds!=null&&age>=e.lifetimeSeconds){finish(group);return;}
  if(age<0){if(!group.announced){const points=group.points||getPoints(e);if(points){group.points=points;warn(e,points,group.started);group.announced=true;}}return;}
  const inWindow=e.endTimeSeconds==null||internalSeconds<=e.endTimeSeconds+1e-7;
  const stageActive=e.generated||group.stage===stage;
  if(enabled&&inWindow&&stageActive) {
   if(e.repeatSeconds){
    while(group.nextWave<=age+1e-7){group.waves.push({index:0,points:null,start:group.nextWave});group.nextWave+=e.repeatSeconds;}
   }else if(group.nextWave===0){group.waves.push({index:0,points:group.points,start:0});group.nextWave=Infinity;}
  }
  if(!inWindow||!stageActive){group.waves=[];if(e.lifetimeSeconds==null){ended.add(e.id);groups.delete(e.id);}return;}
  for(const wave of group.waves){
   if(!enabled)break;
   wave.points??=getPoints(e);
   if(!wave.points)continue;
   const due=e.spawnDuration?Math.min(e.count,1+Math.floor(Math.max(0,age-wave.start)/e.spawnDuration*e.count)):e.count;
   while(wave.index<due){
    const types=Array.isArray(e.enemy)?e.enemy:[e.enemy];
    const type=types[wave.index%types.length];
    const runtime={...e,stage:group.stage,internalSeconds,remainingLife:e.lifetimeSeconds==null?null:Math.max(0,e.lifetimeSeconds-age)};
    if(!spawn(runtime,{...wave.points[wave.index],enemyType:type}))break;
    wave.index++;
   }
  }
  group.waves=group.waves.filter(w=>w.index<e.count);
  if(!e.repeatSeconds&&!group.waves.length&&group.nextWave===Infinity&&e.lifetimeSeconds==null){ended.add(e.id);groups.delete(e.id);}
 }
 return {
  get activeSeconds(){return active;},get activeGroups(){return groups.size;},get generatedSlots(){return index;},
  update(internalSeconds,delta,{stage,enabled=true}={}){
   active+=Math.max(0,delta);
   const allow=enabled&&campaignEventSettings.enabled;
   for(const event of chart){

        pendingStageTransition = next.mapId;

/** Update and render only the active avatar; the inactive character stays hidden. */
function animate(time) {
  const delta = previousTime === undefined ? 0 : Math.min((time - previousTime) / 1000, 0.05);
  previousTime = time;
  mapAudio?.update(delta);
  const activeCharacter = characters[selected];
  levelUpMenu?.update();
  survivalClock.advance(delta, isGameplayPaused(), !isPlayerDefeated(activeCharacter));
  if (endlessMode && isPlayerDefeated(activeCharacter)) {
    const result = runScore.complete({character: activeCharacter, elapsedSeconds:survivalClock.seconds,
      stage:currentMap,endless:true,hardcore:activeCharacter.hardcore === true});
    if (result) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('run-score-calculated',{detail:result}));
  }
  const direction = isGameplayPaused() ? undefined : getMovementDirection();
  if (!isGameplayPaused()) {
    // Queue progression until any existing background ripple finishes; never lose a boss-clear transition.
    if (pendingStageTransition && !mapTransition?.active && switchMap(pendingStageTransition)) {
      pendingStageTransition = null;
    }
    skillCasting?.update(delta);
    updateDamageNumbers(delta);
    playerStatsTools?.update();
    advanceDamageFlash(characters[selected], delta);

## Spreadsheet (Workbook) Complexity: Workbook Structure & Formulas

Keep the workbook simple, especially for focused tasks. A focused task produces a simple analysis, report or tracker for a specific question or workflow. It needs one main output, supported by the necessary inputs and calculations. â€œFocusedâ€ describes the scope of the task, not the number of source records.

Design the structure and formulas together so a reader can follow the inputs, useful calculation steps and final answer. Put summaries and main outputs first, show the work behind them, and avoid tabs or formulas that only repeat finished results. Keep separate schedules and output views when they serve distinct needs. Preserve required detail, the supplied template and the requested edit scope.

## Workbook Structure

### Tab Types & Relationships

Tab types describe the role each part of the workbook plays. They do not require separate tabs. A simple workbook can combine inputs, assumptions, builds and outputs in clearly labeled sections on one worksheet.

**Inputs/Sources and Assumptions feed Builds; Builds calculate results and feed Outputs.** These relationships describe how calculations flow, not the physical tab order. The same rules apply when roles share a tab.

**Input / Sources** contain the data the workbook starts from. Keep dedicated raw source or Actuals areas intact, with original values and source meaning separate from prepared calculations. Cleaning, mapping and source summaries may have their own labeled areas with clear provenance. Put business calculations, including historical calibration from actuals, in the build. Raw source data does not read results back from downstream areas.

**Assumptions** hold the editable drivers and controls used by the builds. When cases are needed, keep one authoritative Case selector on Cover or Assumptions. Group each driver with its `Active Selection` row first, followed by its labeled case inputs, such as Base and Downside, sharing the same period columns. Prefer these driver groups to separate whole-case blocks for new designs. The build links directly to each period's active input. Preserve a supplied layout during narrow edits, and do not add cases or a separate tab when the task does not need them.

Changing the Case selector updates the active forecast assumptions for each period. The same build keeps linking to those active cells and recalculates with the selected values. Outputs update from the build results while historical actuals remain unchanged.

When cases are used, display the selected case on each worksheet by linking to the authoritative selector. Keep only one editable selector; distinguish source actuals and separately labeled comparison cases from the active forecast.

In historical periods, the active assumption row may link to ratios or other measures calculated from actuals in a build. Show that history once, aligned with the build's historical period columns, to help the user set forecast assumptions. The forecast active row selects the chosen case's assumptions and feeds the build. Forecast results must not feed back into the assumptions driving that same forecast. Historical calibration is a business calculation, not a terminal Check/Audit result.

**Build** tabs pull source inputs and assumptions to combine historical analysis, current results and/or a forecast. Bring the relevant inputs and applicable assumptions into clearly labeled rows or columns, then calculate the results on the build. Keep periods aligned and chronological. Show meaningful steps, subtotals and totals so readers can follow the logicâ€”for example, headcount and compensation driving personnel cost, or revenue less COGS producing gross profit. Each step should do useful work. Do not hide the whole calculation in one dense formula or make the build merely repeat finished results from elsewhere.

For a simple calculation, a small labeled assumption block can sit beside it. For a larger build, link important drivers from their control area and show the useful calculation steps. Use one set of forecast schedules driven by the active assumptions, organized by the business sequence, such as revenue, headcount, vendors and cash. Do not mirror the Assumptions grid, add Case columns or parallel named-case forecasts, or apply the selector only to finished results.

A requested case comparison still needs each case's correctly evaluated results. If the requested simultaneous current results cannot be produced with the supported single-build design, explain the limitation and agree on the calculation or refresh method before building the comparison. Do not omit it, link both cases to the active result, or silently substitute snapshots, `TABLE`, arrays, dense formulas or a hidden second build. Preserve explicit user/template requirements and the separately authorized native-feature and capture workflows below.

**Output / Summary** tabs consolidate the builds and tell the main story. These might be named â€œOverview,â€ â€œSummary,â€ â€œExec Summaryâ€ or â€œDashboard,â€ depending on the task. Bring across finished build results, show how matching totals roll into higher-level totals and put the main summary above the detail. Readers should be able to trace a headline result to its supporting build without finding the same calculation repeated elsewhere. Keep input retrieval, case selection and detailed business logic in the owning build/control area. Do not route forecast results through Assumptions before presenting them. Historical references used to set drivers and linked case/period displays remain allowed.

**Check / Audit** tabs review source data and builds for completeness, consistency and reconciliation. They may calculate their own diagnostics, but do not own business calculations or feed assumptions, builds or outputs. Nothing outside the check/audit area should depend on its results.

**Cover, if useful** gives a complex workbook a simple front page, especially for recurring or shared workflows. Include the company/project name or available logo, workbook title and relevant period or as-of date, with generous whitespace and restrained branding. Place it first. Keep analysis and methodology off the cover. Skip it for focused tasks or when the main output provides enough context.

For complex workbooks, use a separate `ReadMe` only when source choices, joins, scoring or refresh steps need more explanation than nearby notes. Explain the method and material limitations without repeating outputs or giving a tab tour. Put it last. Multiple sources alone do not require one.

Apply [Style guidance](style_guidelines.md) to these tab and section roles, so formatting helps readers distinguish the main answer, editable inputs and supporting calculations.

### Tab Names

Use concise names that describe each tab's purpose, such as `Check` or `Audit` for a reconciliation tab. Preserve established names during unrelated edits. For new forecast work, use `Forecast review` for review checks, `Forecast variance` for comparisons with a prior forecast, or `Sensitivity` for assumption tests. Do not label these tabs or views `Movement` or `Forecast movement`.

### Tab Order & Progression

For a new workbook or authorized redesign, start with one clear primary view that answers the task. Start with one tab, or two when the original source needs to stay separate, for focused tasks such as a department budget versus actuals report, a peer-company valuation comparison, a weekly marketing campaign report, an appointment-capacity tracker or a research measurement log with unit conversions. Preserve required source tabs and dependencies. Put the requested summary above the supporting detail and calculations. Add another tab only for a distinct source, calculation, reader or workflow need; do not create a separate tab for every role. Keep review commentary, refresh instructions and documentation beside the relevant work when they do not need a separate workflow.

Keep separate schedules when the work requires them, such as revenue, payroll, depreciation and debt builds in a financial model. One or two tabs is a starting point for the examples above, not a limit on every workbook. Do not shrink text, hide necessary calculations or discard records to meet a tab count or fit one printed page. Preserve the supplied template and existing architecture during narrow edits.

| Domain and task | Do: one output tab | Don't: create extra output/build tabs by default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Finance / FP&A: one department's monthly budget versus actuals | On `Budget vs Actuals`, tab name `BvA`, show total spend and variance at the top, with category-level budget, actuals and variance calculations below. | Separate Summary, Dashboard, Scenarios and Assumptions tabs for this report. |
| Financial modeling: peer-company valuation comparison from supplied data | On `Comparable Companies`, tab name `Comps`, show the requested multiple summaries at the top, with peer-company inputs and calculated multiples below. | A DCF, debt schedule or full three-statement model when the task only asks for comparable-company analysis. |
| Marketing: weekly campaign spend and cost per lead | On `Campaigns`, show total spend, leads and overall cost per lead at the top, with campaign detail below. Calculate overall cost per lead from the matching totals. | One output tab per campaign, a duplicate dashboard or an attribution model that wasn't requested. |
| Healthcare administration: appointment capacity by clinic | On `Appointments`, tab name `Appts`, show available slots, bookings and overall utilization at the top, with clinic and period detail below. Calculate overall utilization from the matching totals. | A separate dashboard, clinical alerts or a payroll schedule for an appointment report. |
| Scientific research: measurement log with required unit conversions and a requested summary | On `Measurements`, show the requested results at the top, with original observations, units and required conversions below. | Separate Protocol, Processing, Calculations and Checks tabs, or statistical tests that the task does not require. |

One output worksheet can contain several useful sections. Keep original sources and substantial builds separate when needed; do not create multiple output tabs for the same answer.

For a file with multiple tabs, the physical left-to-right order is **Outputs â†’ Builds â†’ Inputs/Sources/Internal**, with a separate **Assumptions** control panel kept easy to reach, usually just after the primary output and before build tabs. Covers, key outputs (executive summary, financial statements, etc.) belong toward the left; working builds sit in the middle when needed; data, sources, inputs and internal documentation sit toward the right. A two-tab workbook has Output on the left and Input on the right. The logical calculation flow is Source/Input and Assumptions â†’ Build â†’ Output; a visible control panel may sit to the left of its builds. Do not confuse tab position with calculation sequence. Within a horizontal build, factors may feed intermediate results from left to right; preserve chronological period columns. Within a single worksheet, inputs and supporting calculations below can feed the main answer above. Preserve an intentional user/reference layout; do not reorganize a narrow edit to enforce this default.

#### Checks and Audit

Checks/Audit are terminal review areas and are not required for focused tasks. They read source/build evidence and may calculate or summarize their own diagnostics within that area. No formula outside a terminal check/audit area may use its results, directly or through helpers, names or dynamic references. This includes assumptions, business calculations, summaries, presented outputs, displayed statuses and output gates. Keep necessary input validation in the owning input/build logic; checks observe it independently. When separate tabs are useful, keep Checks/Audit and internal documentation toward the right. In complex workbooks, a divider such as `Internal >>` can group them with source data; follow [Style guidance](style_guidelines.md) for divider and child-tab colors. Preserve useful supplied controls and notes, but do not add separate tabs for a few lines.


### Build Structure and Formula Flow

Arrange labeled rows and columns so a reader can follow starting data, assumptions, useful calculation steps, subtotals and results. Follow the physical layout above; the logical sequence of inputs to results does not require every build to run from top to bottom.

- **Row progression:** make the useful business steps visible, such as quantity Ã— rate, capacity used Ã· capacity available, or a balance plus its movements. Link the clean input and applicable assumption into their own labeled rows, then calculate the result on that build. Do not add trivial steps just to create more rows.
- **Active assumptions:** select the active assumptions once in the control area and link each period's cells directly into the same build. Do not bypass the active row, repeat case selection across schedules, put a forecast inside Assumptions or maintain parallel case builds. Resolve a required comparison's calculation and refresh method as described in [Tab Types & Relationships](#tab-types--relationships).
- **Historical reference:** Assumptions may link to historical ratios calculated from actuals in a build to help set forecast drivers. Trace the cells: this actuals-only reference must not create a feedback loop from the forecast into its own assumptions.
- **Column progression:** keep comparable items, scenarios and periods aligned. Use the shared headers and controls described in [Anchoring](#anchoring) and [Dates and Time Periods](#dates-and-time-periods), rather than repeating them beside each calculation.
- **Roll-forwards:** show opening balance, relevant movements and closing balance. Normally link each new period's opening balance to the prior period's closing balance, preserving the model's actual timing and conventions.
- **Reuse:** keep one place that owns each calculation, then link matching results into summaries and useful output views. Apply the matching-input, period, unit, rounding and override conditions in [Formula Construction](#formula-construction).

A tab that only repeats linked values from another tab or workbook is a red flag. Build tabs should perform useful calculations and show the steps. Output tabs should bring results together and calculate relevant subtotals or totals where needed. A useful output may link directly to completed build results without adding new calculations. Keep a linking-only tab when it serves a clear source, import or reporting need; otherwise, combine or remove it within the authorized scope. Do not invent calculations merely to justify a distinct reader view.

### Workbook Structure Examples

| Example | Do | Don't |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1. Simple action tracker | Use one `Actions` tab with owner, due date, status and the requested totals above the table. | Add Cover, Readme, Inputs, Dashboard and Checks tabs around a small task list. |
| A2. Newly designed monthly activity report | Keep Month as a column in one activity table; use that table directly or add a linked summary tab to its left. | Copy the same layout into Jan, Feb and Mar tabs when separate monthly sheets are not required. |
| A3. Compare several teams or campaigns | Keep the comparison in one table with a team/campaign field and the requested measures. | Create a separate nearly identical report tab for each team and make the reader assemble the comparison. |
| A4. A few shared assumptions | Put a short labeled rate/assumption block to the left of the working calculation, or below the results on one worksheet. | Create Setup and Assumptions tabs for three cells, or duplicate editable copies of the same rate. |
| A5. A requested scenario comparison | Group each driver's Active Selection and case inputs together. Keep one active build. Agree on any required comparison's calculation and refresh method, and label retained results accurately. | Maintain parallel case forecasts, omit the comparison or affected dependencies, link both cases to the active result, or use `TABLE` or snapshots as an ordinary shortcut. Do not add unneeded scenarios. Preserve explicitly required native sensitivity or [capture workflows](#circular-references-and-iterative-calculation). |
| A6. Explain a one-page operating calculation | Put People needed at the top, the work/capacity calculation beneath it, and Requests and Minutes per request below. Let the lower inputs feed the answer above. | Scatter each step across a different tab, bury the answer at the bottom, or show only an unexplained staffing result. |
| A7. Present an existing calculation | In a new multi-tab workbook, put Outputs on the left, Builds in the middle and Sources/Inputs on the right. Link the output to the completed build; on one worksheet, show that output above its build. Keep each editable control authoritative in one place; preserve an intentional front-end selector. | Put the primary output after internal source tabs, duplicate the same editable control in several places, create an unintended circular calculation, or rebuild the same calculation in the summary. |
| A8. Reconcile a small import | Put an independent comparison near the relevant table. Use a Checks/Audit tab only if needed, and keep it a terminal reader of sources and builds. | Add a full control dashboard for one useful tie-out, or make the build, summary or output gate read a Checks/Audit result. |
| A9. Keep source context usable | Document each source once alongside the relevant input data, following [Citation Requirements](#citation-requirements). Retain essential period/unit labels, required row-level source columns and intact source tabs. | Repeat filenames and source explanations across builds and outputs, hide essential context in cell notes, or create Sources, Notes, Methodology and Version History tabs for a one-off analysis with one source. |
| A10. Summarize a long source table | Keep all required records intact and make the primary view compact. Use a separate source tab when it improves use or preserves the import. | Drop rows, hide needed calculations or make text tiny so all the evidence fits on one page. |
| A11. A production plan with distinct schedules | Keep materials, line-capacity and staffing schedules separate when their inputs, time grains or update owners differ; place the primary output plan to the left of those builds, with supporting data/inputs farther right. | Merge incompatible schedules just to stay within two tabs, or repeat their calculations in the summary. |
| A12. A narrow edit to an existing workbook | Change the requested cells and affected dependencies, preserving established tabs, native features and layout. | Normalize, merge, rename or remove existing tabs just because a new workbook could be simpler. |
| A13. Several thin tabs around one calculation | For a new capacity plan, keep the input factors, meaningful work/capacity calculation and requested result together in one view or two useful tabs. A Build should contribute the steps shown in F13. | Create seven tabs that mostly repeat the same central range, with nominal Build tabs doing no distinct work. Putting that central calculation on Checks/Audit is also a dependency failure. |
| A14. More than one output view | Keep an operator detail view and a manager summary when their fields, level of detail or workflow differ. Both may link to the same owning build, as in F14. | Copy the same table into Summary, Dashboard, Report and Executive tabs without a distinct reader need, or invent new calculations just to make each tab look different. |


## Formulas

Apply these rules to newly added or edited formulas and their affected dependencies. Follow the user's preferences and supplied template; preserve unrelated formulas and layout during narrow edits. Design formulas to support the workbook structure above: the reader should be able to follow the inputs, useful calculation steps and final answer.

### Formula Construction

- Use direct references, familiar functions and meaningful intermediate calculations. Follow [Build Structure and Formula Flow](#build-structure-and-formula-flow) to show the work; do not hide an entire build in one dense formula or add trivial helpers just to make formulas shorter.
- Keep raw data, editable assumptions, mappings and business rules in labeled cells or tables. Mathematical, index and control constants may remain in formulas. Keep calculated results as formulas so they update with their inputs.
- Fixed cutoffs or categories from the user's request can appear directly in formulas when result labels state the rule. For example, label `COUNTIFS(B2:B100,">1000")` as `Invoices over $1,000`, without adding an input cell for `1000`. Use one labeled input cell when the cutoff is user-adjustable or serves as a shared assumption across different calculations.
- Calculate a shared result once and reuse it when the inputs, period, units, rounding and overrides match. Keep independent reconciliations independent.
- Use consistent formulas across comparable rows and periods, while preserving intentional differences such as [historical versus forecast logic](domain_guidance/financial_models.md#periods-assumptions-and-scenarios), one-off adjustments and overrides.
- Keep business calculations in the owning build and necessary input guards with their inputs or dependent build logic, following the [terminal Checks/Audit rule](#checks-and-audit). Do not invent business restrictions or wrap ordinary calculations in repeated workbook-wide validation gates. For example, use `=SUM(I11:I12)` for a valid total; do not add an `IF` that rejects a negative result unless the business rule requires it.

### Anchoring

Use `$` to fix only the part of a reference that must stay in place when a formula is copied. Anchor shared **rows, columns or individual cells** so the workbook can reuse one period header, assumption block, item column or Case selector instead of repeating it beside every calculation.

| Reference | What stays fixed | Useful pattern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `C8` | Neither row nor column | A quantity that moves with the calculation when copied across or down. |
| `C$4` | Row 4 | Read each column's period from one shared header row; copying across advances the period, copying down keeps that header. |
| `$A8` | Column A | Read each row's item or category from one shared column; copying down advances the item, copying across keeps its label. |
| `$B$3` | Cell B3 | Reuse one fixed conversion rate or Case selector throughout the applicable calculation. |

For example, `=SUMIFS(Amount,Month,C$4,Item,$A8)` reads the period above and the item at the left. Copied one column right it uses `D$4`; copied one row down it uses `$A9`. The aligned named ranges represent the source columns; they do not require named ranges in the delivered workbook.

A period-specific assumption should move with its period: `=C8*C$3` becomes `=D8*D$3` when copied across. A single assumption shared by every period should stay fixed: `=C8*$B$3` becomes `=D8*$B$3`. Choose between them from the model's meaning, not by adding `$` everywhere. Use keyed lookups when source and destination orders differ; anchoring cannot make mismatched row positions equivalent. Quote cross-sheet names, for example `='Build'!E14`.

### Dates and Time Periods

- When calculations depend on a reporting date, use the date specified by the task or source. Use TODAY() only when calculations should update with the current date. Use a fixed reporting date when results should remain tied to a particular date. Label any assumed date. Preserve source deadlines and flag conflicts with derived deadlines.
- Review the template's calendar, period layout and source grain before building formulas. Use real dates where the source supports them, with number formats for display; do not invent a missing reporting year. Derive period filters and labels from the shared header rather than hardcoding months in individual formulas.
- For a new `Week of` label, use the week's first business day as the underlying date: Monday by default, moved forward for holidays only when a holiday calendar is supplied. Follow an explicit source/template week convention. Do not invent holidays or relabel a week-ending date as a week start.
- When several time scales are needed and the template does not prescribe a layout, place the broader summaries to the left and finer detail to the right: **Annual | Quarterly | Monthly | Weekly**. Include only the time scales needed for the task. Keep periods chronological from left to right within each group; use the supplied fiscal calendar and week convention.
- Separate different time scales with narrow, blank, unfilled spacer columns; do not extend formatting down the entire column. Do not add a spacer merely between actual and forecast months in one continuous schedule. Align matching period columns across Assumptions, builds and summaries where practical. When recent actuals help set drivers, include that historical reference on Assumptions in the same period column as the build, followed by the matching forecast periods. Within a continuous schedule, use one shared period header rather than repeating identical date rows above every subsection. Keep it visible when useful; separate tables with different column meanings may need their own headers, and print titles can repeat headers on printed pages.
- Match each period to its own assumptions and data. Roll detail into summaries using the right calculation: sum additive amounts, use the appropriate ending balance for stocks, and calculate ratios or weighted averages from the relevant components. Do not sum monthly percentages or double-count weeks that cross month boundaries.

For a monthly summary of daily dates, with `C4` holding the first day of the month and aligned source ranges, use `=SUMIFS(Amount,Date,">="&C$4,Date,"<"&EDATE(C$4,1),Item,$A8)`. The next-month exclusive upper bound includes the full last day, including timestamps. Equality to `C$4` is appropriate only when the source already stores that same monthly key.

### Choosing Formulas and Excel Tools

- **Totals and products:** use `SUM` over the relevant detail for total rows. Use `PRODUCT` for a result built by multiplying a range of numeric factors, or direct multiplication for a simple two-cell calculation. Use `SUMPRODUCT` for a sum of matching quantity Ã— rate pairs or a weighted calculation. Keep ranges aligned and bounded; do not include both subtotals and their detail. Check required factors first: `PRODUCT` ignores blank/text cells in a referenced range, which can make missing inputs look like a valid result.
- **Conditional counts, sums and averages:** prefer `COUNTIFS`, `SUMIFS` and `AVERAGEIFS` for new formulas, even with one criterion, so another condition can be added consistently. Avoid choosing `COUNTIF`, `SUMIF` or `AVERAGEIF` for new work by default; preserve a valid existing/template convention during a narrow edit. This preference does not prohibit an ordinary `IF` condition.
- **Lookups:** `INDEX/MATCH`, `VLOOKUP` and `XLOOKUP` are all useful. Follow the user's preference and the workbook's established approach where it works. Make exact versus approximate matching intentional, handle missing keys explicitly and confirm whether duplicate keys should be rejected, matched once or aggregated. Do not substitute a first-match lookup for a required sum.
- **Conditional logic:** use a short `IF` for a simple choice. Nested `IF` formulas are appropriate when they express necessary, understandable logic, including advanced Finance calculations. For a long list of categories or editable rules, prefer a mapping table or labeled steps. Preserve rule order, boundaries, gaps and the unmatched case; do not replace useful business logic merely to reduce nesting.
- **Formula choices to avoid:** do not introduce `LET`, array/spill formulas, `MAP`, `REDUCE` or `LAMBDA`. Use familiar formulas and labeled intermediate steps. Normal range arguments in functions such as `SUMIFS` and `SUMPRODUCT` remain appropriate, as do the lookup, `INDIRECT`, `OFFSET` and `CHOOSE` patterns below. Preserve required existing/template behavior and do not rewrite unrelated formulas during a narrow edit. Formula length alone is not the test: the reader must be able to understand and extend the calculation.
- **Sensitivity analysis:** For requested one- or two-input sensitivity analyses, use native What-If Data Tables where supported when the alternative would duplicate complex model logic in the sensitivity grid. Simple, self-contained calculations may use ordinary formulas. For requested Excel financial-model sensitivities, default to native What-If Data Tables where supported; follow [Finance Guidance](domain_guidance/financial_models.md#valuation-and-returns) for model links and verification. Do not introduce `TABLE` into an ordinary forecast or case comparison, or manufacture a second varying input with a metric selector. Excel supports one or two varying inputs; the current Artifact Tool supports only two-variable tables, with both input cells on the tableâ€™s worksheet. Read [Data Tables](artifact_tool_docs/DATA_TABLES.md) before creating one. Two inputs test one output across their combinations; use separate tables for additional outputs. If the requested native design is unsupported, explain the limitation before agreeing on a formula-based design or change-input/recalculate/restore process. Label captured results and their refresh method. Ordinary case comparisons follow the single-build and comparison boundary above.

An Excel Table, PivotTable and What-If Data Table are different features. Check the chosen tool and destination's support. If a requested native feature cannot be created or preserved, explain the limitation before substituting a formula or static result. Keep API setup and feature-specific execution details in the relevant tool reference.
